mechanism: closure/fork structure supervision on a fixed E16 x H16 product quantizer

computations.name: split
computations.definition: latent split into 16 Euclidean and 16 hyperbolic tangent coordinates

computations.name: ball_map
computations.definition: H mapped into the curvature-1 Poincare ball by h*tanh(||h||)/||h||; only saturated tails are pulled back

computations.name: cumulative_positions
computations.definition: one real quantization forward yields one selection and three cumulative positions q1=c1, q2=c1(+)c2, q3=c1(+)(c2(+)c3); no re-quantization, no second gather

computations.name: triples
computations.definition: closed triangle h=1 on all three pairs; open wedge: observed pairs h=1, unobserved B-C pair h=2

computations.name: level_objective
computations.definition: per-level objective L_l = E_T[(1/3) sum_{a<b} (d^2/(s^2 h^2) - 1)^2]

computations.name: prefix_objective
computations.definition: prefix objective L_prefix = (L_1+L_2+L_3)/3 with the same triples, targets, s and lambda

computations.name: scale
computations.definition: scale: median of sqrt(clamp_min(d_M^2,1e-8)) over h=1 pairs on a fixed TRAIN sample, once after codebook init on the last level, frozen for all levels; empty/undefined samples are degenerate

inputs.triples: centre and two partners from the TRAIN graph

outputs.positions: right-nested product readback: E sum plus H = c1 (+)(c2 (+) c3) read through log0; the decoder consumes that log0 readback

parameters.weight_rule: one two-block gradient-norm budget over the complete prefix target: lambda = min over {encoder, all codebooks} of ||grad_base||/||grad_prefix||; decoder excluded; no per-layer weights, no ratio constant, no sweep

gradient_rules.rule: encoder: one unit straight-through per level, q^(l)=R_l+z-sg(z); proxy Jacobian is I at every level
codebooks: only the native readback's continuous Jacobian including the indirect path through earlier codewords; no additional residual STE path
quantisation loss keeps its own gather path to the codebooks

training_integration.behaviour_on: structure term added with its calibrated lambda
training_integration.geometry_on: product geodesic in assignment and loss; otherwise the Euclidean control
training_integration.prefix_objective: L = L_base + lambda*L_prefix; lambda calibrated once before any optimizer step with the two-block budget; lambda_mean=3*lambda_sum only under identical s, state, sample and blocks, and does not make last-level supervision equivalent
training_integration.loss: L = L_base + lambda * L_prefix, where L_base = reconstruction MSE + commitment
training_integration.reconstruction: decoder consumes the log0 readback of the right-nested composition
training_integration.optimizer: AdamW on the frozen budget; no early stopping, no per-layer weights

conventions.distance: sqrt of the product squared distance

switches.behaviour_off: structure term is not added; reconstruction/commitment unchanged
switches.geometry_off: assignment and structure use the Euclidean distance instead of the product geodesic
switches.both_on: structure term with the product geodesic
switches.prefix: behaviour-off removes the structure objective; geometry-off switches selection, residual and readback to the tangent path together; both-on is the only trained arm

excluded.reason: an argmin is not differentiable; the surrogate carries the gradient but cannot be symbolically compared
iterative normalisation with an argmax at the end; discrete output, covered by the assignment-rule check and the suites
discrete sampling; the contract covers the objective it feeds, the sampler is covered by its own tests

excluded: hard argmin/argmax selection is not differentiable
the STE proxy is verified as a declared rule, not by finite differences

distance_surface.note: aligned with contract.calls[name=mixed_distance]; both use the stable squared differences

args.name: points
args.domain: three points, each (E tangent, H tangent); box sampler, radius 0.3

args.name: u
args.domain: target offsets; h_k = 1 + tanh(u_k) > 0; box sampler, radius 0.5

args.name: scale
args.domain: positive median-distance scale; box sampler, radius 0.5

continuous_surface.callable_note: the adapter reshapes points to (batch, 3, 2) and calls mixed_geometry.reference_surface; it is the same phi form the production distance uses
continuous_surface.limitations: the surface is the E1 x H1 per-point subspace of the full E16 x H16 distance; the embedding into 32 dimensions and the vector-norm cross ratio of H16 are not represented here, so this is a reduced reference surface, not a full-dimensional equivalence claim

statements: L_l = mean over TRAIN triples of (e_l(centre, a) + e_l(centre, b) + e_l(a, b)) / 3
prefix_surface.note: one shared s, one lambda, one TRAIN triple set with the three pair targets; no next-item objective, no per-layer scale, no second gather.  The implemented training term is the last-layer structure loss, not this prefix objective
prefix_surface.full_space: E16 x H16: Euclidean part is a squared difference. H part: ball point b = to_ball(t) = tanh(|t|)/|t| * t; t_cross = |b-b'|^2 / ((1-|b|^2)(1-|b'|^2)) (this direction, NOT its reciprocal); phi(t) = asinh(sqrt(t))^2 and d_M^2 = |e-e'|^2 + phi(t). Standard hyperbolic squared distance is 4*phi; the product term uses phi, so the normalisation is fixed and c=1. A reciprocal cross-ratio would diverge at the legal collision b=b' (t_cross=0) and is wrong.
prefix_surface.residual_and_readback: Let C_l be the selected codeword's tangent coordinates at level l and B_l = code_ball(C_l^H); initial state r_0^E = z^E, r_0^H = to_ball(z^H). Then r_l^E = r_{l-1}^E - C_l^E and r_l^H = (-B_l) mobius_add r_{l-1}^H (Moebius left inverse). The cumulative codeword position of level l is R_l = (sum_{j<=l} C_j^E, log_0(B_1 mobius_add (B_2 mobius_add ... B_l))); the readback is q_l = R_l + z - sg(z). The selection input is the E coordinates of the current residual and log_0 of its H ball, not a whole-space subtraction. Mobius addition and its inverse are defined on the open ball |a|<1; boundary points are excluded. Encoder STE and codebook native Jacobian are stated separately in ste_boundaries.
prefix_surface.ste_boundaries: encoder receives straight-through gradients through each selection; codebooks receive their native readback gradients only; the discrete choice remains the baseline Sinkhorn assignment, not a plain argmin

calibration.s: one shared positive scale from calibrate_structure_scale on the initialised model: the median h=1 pair distance over TRAIN triples; structure.calibrate_scale currently returns 1.0 on an empty sample, which is a known degenerate default and is not a calibrated value
calibration.lambda: one value for the complete prefix objective, calibrated by the two-block rule (encoder; all codebooks merged) from question8 section 4; not the historical checkpoint's value
calibration.budget: frozen optimizer budget; no per-layer weight selection, no scan, no extra seed

coverage_gaps: the reduced E1 x H1 adapter uses h=1+tanh(u) and box sampling; exact h=2 is covered by the real target tests (test_structure.py), not by the reduced adapter
H1 squared-difference identity does not demonstrate H16 non-Euclidean effects
this prefix objective is NOT_IMPLEMENTED in the trainer; only the last-layer structure term runs

rejected_draft_forms.cross_ratio_reciprocal: t_draft=(1-|a|^2)(1-|b|^2)/|a-b|^2 gave 19.007999999999996 where the native t is 0.05260942760942763 for the same ball points, and divides by zero at the legal collision
rejected_draft_forms.euclidean_residual: r_l=r_{l-1}-z_l would give H tangent (0.2,-0.2) instead of the native (0.1868567811974333,-0.22350722788306665); a native readback then recovers with error 0.023069610924273662 instead of 8.3e-17

continuous_surface.expression_note: on the E1 x H1 subface the H16 cross-ratio reduces to sinh(x1-y1)^2 and asinh^2(sqrt(t)) = (x1-y1)^2; the statements use that identity so the declared surface has a finite backward at coincident points

revision.reason: the distance-norm stress (d/(s h) - 1)^2 has a cusp at a collision (q_a == q_b is possible once hard SIDs collide); the squared-distance stress has an exact zero gradient there
revision.delta: objective is now (d_M^2 / (s^2 h^2) - 1)^2 per pair; the target distance is unchanged, the loss and its gradient are not
revision.analytic_reference: for a Euclidean difference x and target a = s h: grad = 4x/a^2 (||x||^2/a^2 - 1); at x = 0 it is exactly 0
revision.prefix_candidate: question8 section 4 equal-weight three-level candidate; DRAFT, not reviewed, not frozen
